hook.line: Sometimes you shake your head and smile at someone, or sigh over the good old days. Spanish has a short exclamation for both, with the demonstrative at the end.

rule:
Normally *este* and *aquel* come before the noun: *aquellos tiempos*. In an exclamation they jump to the end.

*¡Qué* + noun + *este/esta/aquel/aquella...*

With *aquellos*, you look back with warmth: *¡Qué tiempos aquellos!* With *este* or *esta*, you comment on someone in front of you, and it can be admiration: *¡Qué mujer esta!*

The second shape drops the *qué*: *¡Este muchacho!* Then you trail off, shake your head, and add a line. It sounds like fond exasperation.

The tone does the work, so say it as you would in English: *This boy!*
smallPrint: Teachers call this a postposed demonstrative: the demonstrative placed after the noun, which Spanish only allows in exclamations like these.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the demonstrative and type the whole sentence: *¡Qué tiempos ___!* (aquellos or ahora)
yourTurn.why: *Aquellos* looks back at the good old days.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: What a woman she is!
yourTurn.why: *Esta* goes at the end and agrees with *mujer*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: This boy! He never learns.
yourTurn.why: A trailing *este muchacho* is fond exasperation.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: What a man he is!
Type in Spanish: This girl! She's always late.
Make it about the past: *¡Qué tiempos aquellos!* Say: Those were the days!, with días.
yourTurn.why: Swap the noun, keep the shape.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: This child! He never listens.

pitfalls.why: Almost. In this exclamation the demonstrative goes after the noun.
Almost. The demonstrative must match the noun: *mujer* is feminine, so *esta*.

personal: Think of someone you love who drives you a little mad, and say it with *¡Este...!* or *¡Esta...!*.
